source.title: Between MDPs and semi-MDPs: A framework for temporal abstraction in reinforcement learning

confidence_rationale: Foundational warrant that temporal abstraction is a distinct capability (faster credit assignment, structured exploration over a semi-MDP). But silent on where good options come from; demonstrations use hand-specified options. Supports the framework, not a floor->competent number.
failure_signatures: The options framework is silent on option DISCOVERY; its speedups are shown with hand-specified options, so it does not by itself close a floor->competent gap without a source of good options.

mapping.source_claim_statement: An option (initiation set, policy, termination condition) is a temporally-extended closed-loop sub-behaviour usable like a primitive action; planning/learning over the resulting semi-MDP jump value backups across timesteps, giving faster credit assignment and structured exploration.
mapping.ree_translation: Options change the decision granularity and credit-assignment timescale of REE's actor-critic -- orthogonal to a novelty bonus (which changes what states are visited, not the timescale of decision/credit).
mapping.mapping_caveat: The framework requires a source of options; its gridworld demonstrations use hand-specified options, so the floor->competent benefit depends on option discovery (Paper: DIAYN) or hand-design.
mapping.source_context: Tabular RL theory + small gridworld planning demonstrations.

confidence_components.notes: Framework-level support; buildable with hand-specified options as a cheap probe, heavier with learned options.
